title: Agentic engineering platform: gateway, MCP and risk-based review
problem: Give 250+ engineering teams measurable access to LLMs and coding agents without forcing one tool, while controlling cost, governance and delivery risk.
depth: Detailed platform components and governance; limited ROI evidence
technologies_stated: LiteLLM-based gateway (OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex)
internal MCP servers with OAuth ingress filter
facts: A LiteLLM-based gateway proxies model access with pre and post call hooks and prompt-cache checkpoint injection.
A local proxy injects auth headers for coding agents and shows per-model cost and cache usage.
Internal MCP servers sit behind a default OAuth ingress filter; configuration is secret-free via token injection.
About a third of pull requests are classified low-risk and auto-approved; risk rules derive from production incidents, and risk-based approval is reported to cut lead time by 20-40% versus all PRs.
A future agent platform with an identity broker, delegation chains and token vault is described as in progress.
Sandboxing is listed as an unsolved problem.
interpretations: Gateway-first rollout produces the telemetry needed for governance before standardising tools.

decisions.selected: Single gateway, no mandated client tool
decisions.reasoning: Source states goal of measurable access without central mandate and cites difficulty consolidating tools.

decisions.alternatives: Human review for every PR; size limits only
decisions.reasoning: Source reports lead-time reduction and risk rules from incidents.

decisions.selected: Planned identity broker with delegation and token vault
decisions.reasoning: Source lists the broker as being built.

review_exercise: Coding agents increase PR size and complexity. Design controls that preserve review quality without hurting lead time.
lessons: Governance rules should come from incident data.
Agent identity is still an open problem even at mature organisations.
adaptation: Useful template for governing AI-assisted SAP development teams. Independent analysis.
